## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | "Rigorous double-anonymized reviewing policy": identities of reviewer and author are concealed from each other. Author-suggested reviewers are not permitted at any stage; reviewers are not assigned if at the same institution as a co-author or at the funding body |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Not stated on the guidelines page. One SciRev review (n=1) reports being advised to revise and resubmit to a different journal, unexplained |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No: the Web of Science reviewer-credit partnership does not publish the article name, decision or review content |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev average 1.7 rounds (n=5) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Author-suggested reviewers are not permitted (Sage policy, same page) |

> Source: https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr (Wayback snapshot 2025-08-07), section 5.1. Submission via Sage Track / ScholarOne.

### AI Policy

The earlier summary that listed only generative AI is corrected: qualitative-analysis software is also within the disclosure rule |
| **Source URL** | https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr |

## Format

Source for this section: https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr (Wayback snapshot 2025-08-07).

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original Research Studies (fully developed qualitative studies, including mixed methods whose major focus is qualitative); Pearls, Piths, and Provocations (debate, methodological advances, teaching, new ideas; review articles go here); Editorials (generally invited). Pilot studies are not published; literature reviews are not normally published unless they address methodological issues |
| **Word limit** | 8,000 words or fewer, excluding abstract, references and acknowledgements; text in tables and figures counts; online supplementary material does not |
| **Word limit negotiability** | No negotiation route stated |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured, narrative, at most 250 words; keywords beneath it |
| **Reference limit** | No limit on the number of references; APA 7; the guidelines recommend pertinent references only, including earlier QHR work |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed (datasets, podcasts, video, images); core elements must not be placed in supplementary material |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit; tables "sparingly"; do not tabulate individual participant details; images at least 300 dpi (line art 800 dpi) |

| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical qualitative studies dominate: "interview" in 596 of 902 (66.1%), "thematic analysis" 154 (17.1%), the word "theory" alone 176 (19.5%; case-insensitive whole-word match `\btheory\b`, recomputed 2026-11-23 over the same 902 abstracts; the prefix match `\btheor` gives 224, 24.8%, and a broad word); the journal's own description limits original research to qualitative studies. 8 of the 12 most-cited 2021-2026 Crossref records are methodological papers (see Epistemological & Political Leanings) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Qualitative: "quantitative" appears in 19 of 902 (2.1%), "survey/questionnaire" in 20 (2.2%), "mixed method" in 14 (1.6%); mixed methods are accepted only when the major focus is qualitative (guidelines section 1.2) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07) say QHR is "an international, interdisciplinary forum to enhance health and health care and further the development and understanding of qualitative health research", with conceptual, theoretical, methodological and ethical issues about qualitative inquiry also covered. **Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** qualitative interview studies; grounded theory; phenomenology; narrative inquiry; ethnography; participatory and visual methods; methodological and teaching papers in the Pearls, Piths, and Provocations section.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: yes, stated. Authors are asked to judge fit themselves: "Does your proposed submission make a meaningful and strong contribution to qualitative health research literature?" and whether it is useful to readers or practitioners; the editor asks not to receive query letters (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 1.1).
- Review criteria stated for original research: importance, methodological considerations, ethical concerns, depth and coherence of analysis, style, scope (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 2.1); for Pearls, Piths, and Provocations: significance, clarity, rigor, engagement, writing (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 2.2).
- Rigor is shown narratively: "authors should not include qualitative research checklists, such as COREQ"; a narrative approach is expected and "detailed reflections on methodological considerations" (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 3.4).
- Mixed methods: accepted only if the major focus is qualitative; "supplementary component of mixed methods studies often are rejected" (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, sections 1.2 and 2.3).
- Consequences of ignoring it, stated by the journal: QHR "most commonly turns away manuscripts that fall outside the journal's scope, do not make a novel contribution to the literature, lack substantive and/or interpretative depth, require extensive revisions, and/or do not adequately address ethical issues" (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 2.3). Two SciRev rejections (n=2 of 5) were immediate, at 4 and 11 days (https://scirev.org/reviews/qualitative-health-research/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The earlier note that this rejection-reasons text could not be reproduced is resolved: it is on the guidelines page.

### Voice & Style

- Length and format (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07): 8,000 words or fewer excluding abstract, references and acknowledgements; double-spaced, 1-inch margins, Times New Roman 12 point; APA 7 references; abstract unstructured, at most 250 words.
- Structure: authors may use Background, Methods, Results, Discussion or choose their own; the page expects "detailed reflections on methodological considerations" and narrative description of rigor instead of checklists (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 3.4).
- Participant voice: quotations may be linked to participants if anonymised, for example with pseudonyms; demographics are reported in narrative or aggregate form (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 3.4).
- First-person use in abstracts: 400 of 902 (44%) contain "I", "my", "we" or "our" (case-sensitive local match on Crossref abstracts 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23); "reflexiv*" appears in 101 (11.2%). The earlier "5 - reflexive voice expected" rating is not supported by a stated rule; first person appears in under half of abstracts.
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1177/10497323261492958 opens with a participant group ("People with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis face complex choices"); 10.1177/10497323261494477 opens "This qualitative study explored"; 10.1177/10497323261477628 opens "This article examines"; 10.1177/10497323261487317 opens with a field-level claim about large language models; 10.1177/10497323261487330 opens "This article makes a methodological case". Abstracts typically open in third person with the group, setting or claim.

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | A title-page ethical statement must give the ethics board's full name, the approval number and confirmation that participants gave informed consent; the Methods must say whether consent was written or verbal, how and by whom; if no approval was needed, a statement and reason are still required (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/qhr, snapshot 2025-08-07, section 3.2) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | 98 of 911 Crossref records with author lists (10.8%) have a single author; median 4 authors (Crossref, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Not stated on the pages read; no affiliation requirement appears in the guidelines |
| **Data transparency requirement** | No data-availability rule stated on the QHR page; participant identification rules apply (aggregate demographics, pseudonyms) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Title page and cover letter are the only places for identifying information; double-anonymised review (section 3 and 5.1). The cover letter must disclose overlapping or same-dataset work, and copies may be requested |

- Authorship follows ICMJE criteria; writing assistance other than language polishing must be acknowledged (section 5.2-5.3).
- Funding and conflict-of-interest statements are required (sections 5.4-5.5).
- Contributor agreement: an exclusive licence to Sage, with the author retaining copyright (section 6.2); optional Sage Choice open access (section 6.3).
- Archiving: Sage's policy, see Preprint Policy.

**AI-research finding (policy):** SAGE 出版社整體政策:LLM/生成式AI(如ChatGPT)可作為寫作生產力工具(構思結構、摘要、改寫、潤色),不得列為作者。QHR 期刊投稿須知進一步要求:凡使用生成式AI協助構思、研究設計、資料生成、分析協助或呈現研究發現等『構成質性研究要素』的活動,須在正文中明確標示,並在 Acknowledgements 中揭露所用技術名稱、存取時間與用途。允許使用範圍相對寬(涵蓋研究設計/分析輔助),但強制揭露,屬有條件開放而非全面禁止或無限制開放。(2026-11-23: confirmed against the guidelines snapshot; the rule also covers NVivo, ATLAS.ti and Quirkos.)

**AI-research finding (positioning — what the journal accepts now):** 疾病/患病經驗(illness experience)、健康與就醫行為(health and health-seeking behaviors)、照顧者經驗、健康照護之社會文化組織、健康照護政策等議題的質性研究,強調 novelty、方法論嚴謹度與分析深度。(2026-11-23: the guidelines' rejection-reasons paragraph, section 2.3, states novelty, interpretative depth, scope and ethics; the page was readable via the Wayback snapshot.)

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A quantitative-only or pilot study: the guidelines define original research as qualitative studies, accept mixed methods only when qualitatively driven, and do not publish pilot studies (Format table, Framing Requirements).
- Identifying information outside the title page and cover letter: double-anonymised review (Peer Review table; Practical Concerns).
- Missing ethics statement with board name, approval number and consent confirmation (Practical Concerns, IRB row).
- Undisclosed use of generative AI or qualitative-analysis software (AI Policy table).
- Including a qualitative-reporting checklist such as COREQ: the guidelines say not to (Framing Requirements).

### Soft Tax

- 8,000 words including text inside tables and figures (Format table).
- Narrative demonstration of rigor and "detailed reflections on methodological considerations" in place of checklists (Framing Requirements, Voice & Style).
- Cover-letter disclosure of overlapping or same-dataset papers (Practical Concerns).
- Timeline uncertainty: SciRev (n=5) gives 1.8 months to first round and 3.5 months total, but one accepted review shows 25.0 weeks; two immediate rejections took 4 and 11 days (Review Cycle Time). These are anecdotes.

### Best Suited For

- Interview-based qualitative studies of health experience: "interview" in 66.1% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Studies in the frequent topic areas: mental health 17.3%, stigma 9.8%, COVID-19 8.9%, cancer 8.0%, caregiving 7.1% (Sensitive Topics).
- Methodological, teaching or debate papers for the Pearls, Piths, and Provocations section: 8 of the 12 most-cited recent records are methodological (Epistemological & Political Leanings; Format table).
- Phenomenological, narrative and grounded-theory studies: 10.9%, 18.0% and 7.6% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences).

### Not Recommended For

- Stand-alone quantitative health research: "quantitative" appears in 2.1% of abstracts and the guidelines restrict original research to qualitative studies (Methodological Preferences, Format).
- Mixed-methods papers where the qualitative part is minor, or the supplementary arm of a larger study: stated common rejection reason (Framing Requirements).
- Literature reviews that are not methodological: not normally published (Format table).
- Authors who need a predictable decision time: only SciRev anecdotes (n=5) exist (Review Cycle Time).
